items.title: Stop the entry armed gate from stranding an exit
acceptance: An identity-valid EXIT on proven attributable exposure is not blocked by an entry-only armed downgrade.
Operator trading disabled remains a hard block for every mutation including EXIT.
Account, contract, instrument identity and native ownership validation remain mandatory for EXIT.
Exit permission is a distinct, named decision from entry permission in both code and the decision packet.
supported_actions and any exit-permission field agree with what the coordinator will actually submit.
Fixtures cover exit during quote staleness, quiet tape, reconciliation lag, and recovery-blocked state.
evidence: 2026-07-28 audit src/execution/coordinator.ts handleExit: EXIT returns shadowed/exit_verified_not_submitted whenever gatewayModePermitsLiveOrders(packet.execution.gateway_mode) is false.
2026-07-28 audit src/execution/gateway-mode.ts armedGateReasons: armed degrades on quote_stale, reconciliation_not_current, and order_flow_no_trades_60s.

Net effect: an open position cannot be closed by Hermes exactly when quotes thin out, the tape goes quiet, or reconciliation lags. On an account with a hard trailing loss floor that is the wrong failure direction.
docs/AUTHORITY.md permits deterministic rejection for factual execution invalidity; a quiet tape or a stale quote does not make closing an existing position factually invalid.

The sibling NinjaTrader rail already carries this contract: GL-AI-08 requires that an identity-valid attributable EXIT bypass entry-only license, compliance, session, and new-risk gates while AI-disabled stays a hard block.
packet.execution.supported_actions always advertises EXIT, so the packet currently overstates what the gateway will submit.
items.stop_line: This widens live-order authority. It requires explicit operator approval before implementation, and bounded shadow proof before any armed run.

items.title: Move the quiet-tape armed gate out of Glitch or justify it as a venue boundary
acceptance: order_flow_no_trades_60s is either removed from the armed gate and published as pure evidence, or documented as an authoritative venue/account boundary with a named source.
The decision is recorded against the docs/AUTHORITY.md change test with an explicit answer to each of its four questions.
Whatever remains in the gate is proven not to block an exit, per TS-AUDIT-02.
Hermes still receives the full rolling tape so it can decline a thin market by judgment.
evidence: 2026-07-28 audit src/execution/gateway-mode.ts: a 60s window with trade_count <= 0 downgrades armed to degraded_armed and suppresses live orders.

docs/AUTHORITY.md forbids Glitch from encoding a fixed strategy, indicator trigger, setup checklist, or entry score, and its change test says a rule whose removal would merely let Hermes exercise judgment belongs in cognition.
A quiet tape is a market condition, not a factual execution error: quantity, identity, protection geometry, and account capacity are all still provable with zero prints in the window.
docs/TOPSTEP-NATIVE.md already states new_exposure_technically_supported reflects venue completeness rather than model conviction, which this gate contradicts.
Absent market-hub prints are separately visible through market_stream_state and the order_flow observation, so removing the gate loses no evidence.
items.stop_line: Doctrine decision for the operator. Do not silently relax the gate as part of unrelated work.

items.title: Reconcile instrument scoping across the entry admission guards
acceptance: Position and working-order admission guards use one documented scope, or each states why its scope differs.
Any narrowing is justified against provable ownership rather than convenience.
The account-wide Topstep contract ceiling stays account-wide.
Fixtures cover a working order on a second contract in the same account.
evidence: 2026-07-28 audit src/risk/risk-engine.ts: position_addition_not_implemented tests snapshot.instrumentOpenContracts (instrument-scoped) while working_order_ownership_unresolved tests snapshot.openOrders.length, which venue-state builds filtered by accountId only and not by contractId.
A working order on any other contract in the account therefore blocks entry on the configured contract, while an open position on that other contract does not.

Latent under the current single-contract acceptance scope; it becomes live behaviour as soon as a second Topstep contract is configured, which docs/TOPSTEP-NATIVE.md treats as a configuration change rather than an architecture change.
Narrowing the order guard would loosen a safety admission check, so it needs proven per-contract ownership first.
items.stop_line: Do not loosen the working-order guard before per-contract ownership is provable.
